blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int x(7x^{2}+8)^{9}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh sawal power wala hai: ek bracket \((7x^{2}+8)\) power 9 par hai aur bahar \(x\) se multiply ho raha hai.
Diya kya hai? Sirf integral. Find kya karna hai? Is ka antiderivative (yani woh function jis ka derivative yeh integrand ho).
Pehle andar wale hisse ka derivative sochiye: \(7x^{2}+8\) ka derivative \(14x\) hai. Bahar wala \(x\) bilkul isi ka hissa hai, sirf 14 ka farq hai.
Jab bhi andar wale ka derivative bahar baitha ho, substitution sab se aasaan rasta hai.
Plan: \(u = 7x^{2}+8\) rakhenge, \(u\) mein power rule lagayenge, phir wapas \(x\) likhenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int x(7x^{2}+8)^{9}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: substitution (change of variable). Jab andar wale expression ka derivative bahar factor ki shakal mein maujood ho, to andar wale ko \(u\) keh dete hain; integral seedha \(\int u^{n}\,du\) ban jata hai jo hum power rule se kar lete hain.

\(u\) chunein aur \(du\) nikalein
\[u = 7x^{2}+8\]
\[du = 14x\,dx\]
\[x\,dx = \dfrac{du}{14}\]
Kyun: integral mein \(x\,dx\) pada hai; usay poora ka poora \(du\) mein badalna zaroori hai, warna integral mein \(x\) aur \(u\) dono mil jayenge aur hal nahi hoga. Is liye \(du = 14x\,dx\) ko 14 se divide kar diya.

Integral ko \(u\) mein likhein
\[\int (7x^{2}+8)^{9}\,x\,dx\]
\[= \int u^{9}\cdot\dfrac{du}{14}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{14}\int u^{9}\,du\]
Kyun: bracket \(u\) ban gaya aur \(x\,dx\) ban gaya \(du/14\). Constant \(\frac{1}{14}\) ko integral ke bahar nikal sakte hain, is se hisaab saaf rehta hai.

Power rule lagayein
\[= \dfrac{1}{14}\cdot\dfrac{u^{10}}{10} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{140}u^{10} + c\]
Kyun: rule hai \(\int u^{n}\,du = \frac{u^{n+1}}{n+1} + c\), jab \(n \ne -1\). Yahan \(n = 9\), to power ek barh kar 10 hui aur 10 se divide kiya.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{1}{14}\) wala constant bhoolna aam ghalti hai; phir jawab 14 guna bara aata hai.

Wapas \(x\) likhein
\[= \dfrac{1}{140}(7x^{2}+8)^{10} + c\]
Kyun: \(u\) humne apni sahulat ke liye banaya tha; sawal \(x\) mein tha, is liye jawab bhi \(x\) mein dena hai.

Tasdeeq: jawab ka derivative lein
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{140}(7x^{2}+8)^{10}\Big]\]
\[= \dfrac{10\cdot 14x}{140}(7x^{2}+8)^{9}\]
\[= x(7x^{2}+8)^{9}\]
Kyun: chain rule se derivative lene par asal integrand wapas mil gaya. Integration ka sab se pakka check yahi hai ke jawab ko differentiate karein.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Answer key mein is sawal ke jawab 'Exercise 3.2' ke neeche nahi hain (us heading ke neeche asal mein Exercise 3.5 ke jawab hain). Jawab yahan milenge:
Q1 (i)-(iv): 'EXERCISE 3.1' ke neeche 4 (i)-(iv); Q1 (v): 4 (vi); Q1 (vi): 4 (vii).
Q1 (vii)-(xiii): 'Exercise 3.3' ke neeche 2 (i)-(vii).
Key ka 4 (v), \(\frac{2}{21}(7x+8)^{3/2} + c\), is exercise ke kisi sawal ka jawab nahi hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{x^{2}}{(x^{3}+2)^{5}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan denominator mein \((x^{3}+2)\) ki power 5 hai aur upar \(x^{2}\) hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Socho: \(x^{3}+2\) ka derivative \(3x^{2}\) hai, aur upar \(x^{2}\) pada hai. Bas 3 ka farq hai, jo constant hai aur aasani se adjust ho jata hai.
Is liye \(u = x^{3}+2\) lenge, \(\frac{1}{u^{5}}\) ko \(u^{-5}\) likhenge aur power rule lagayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{x^{2}}{(x^{3}+2)^{5}}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: substitution \(u = x^{3}+2\). Wajah: is ka derivative \(3x^{2}\) numerator \(x^{2}\) se sirf constant 3 mein mukhtalif hai, to poora numerator \(du\) mein badal jayega.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = x^{3}+2\]
\[du = 3x^{2}\,dx\]
\[x^{2}\,dx = \dfrac{du}{3}\]
Kyun: numerator \(x^{2}\,dx\) ko poori tarah \(du\) mein likhna hai, is liye 3 se divide kiya.

Integral ko \(u\) mein likhein
\[\int \dfrac{x^{2}\,dx}{(x^{3}+2)^{5}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\int u^{-5}\,du\]
Kyun: denominator wala \(u^{5}\) upar laane se power negative ho jati hai: \(\frac{1}{u^{5}} = u^{-5}\). Ab yeh seedha power rule ka sawal hai.

Power rule
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{u^{-4}}{-4} + c\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{12}u^{-4} + c\]
Kyun: \(n = -5\) hai, to \(n + 1 = -4\). Power ek barhane ka matlab \(-5\) se \(-4\) hai, \(-6\) nahi.
Dhyan dein: negative power mein bachche aksar \(-5 + 1\) ko \(-6\) likh dete hain; yeh ghalat hai.

Wapas \(x\) likhein
\[= -\dfrac{1}{12}(x^{3}+2)^{-4} + c\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{12(x^{3}+2)^{4}} + c\]
Kyun: jawab sawal ke variable \(x\) mein hona chahiye. Dono shaklein barabar hain; kitab pehli shakal likhti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[-\tfrac{1}{12}(x^{3}+2)^{-4}\Big]\]
\[= -\tfrac{1}{12}(-4)(x^{3}+2)^{-5}(3x^{2})\]
\[= \dfrac{x^{2}}{(x^{3}+2)^{5}}\]
Kyun: chain rule se \(-\frac{1}{12}\cdot(-4)\cdot 3 = 1\) ban gaya aur asal integrand wapas aa gaya.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^{-2}\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein bracket \((1 + \frac{1}{x})\) ki power \(-2\) hai aur saath \(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\) multiply ho raha hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Andar wale ka derivative dekhiye: \(1 + \frac{1}{x}\) ka derivative \(-\frac{1}{x^{2}}\) hai. Yeh doosra factor hi hai, sirf minus sign ka farq hai.
Minus sign se ghabrana nahi; woh bhi ek constant \((-1)\) hai jo bahar aa jata hai.
Plan: \(u = 1 + \frac{1}{x}\), power rule (\(n = -2\)), phir jawab ko simple karna.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int (1+\frac{1}{x})^{-2}\,\frac{1}{x^{2}}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: substitution \(u = 1 + \frac{1}{x}\). Wajah: is ka derivative \(-\frac{1}{x^{2}}\) integrand mein maujood hai (sirf minus ke farq ke saath).

\(u\) chunein
\[u = 1 + \dfrac{1}{x} = 1 + x^{-1}\]
\[du = -x^{-2}\,dx = -\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}\,dx\]
\[\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}\,dx = -du\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{x}\) ko \(x^{-1}\) likh kar power rule se derivative: \(-1\cdot x^{-2}\). Constant 1 ka derivative zero hai.

Integral ko \(u\) mein likhein
\[\int u^{-2}(-du) = -\int u^{-2}\,du\]
Kyun: bracket \(u\) bana aur \(\frac{1}{x^{2}}dx\) bana \(-du\). Minus constant hai, bahar nikal diya.

Power rule
\[= -\dfrac{u^{-1}}{-1} + c = u^{-1} + c\]
Kyun: \(n = -2\) to \(n + 1 = -1\). Upar wala minus aur neeche wala \(-1\) aapas mein cancel ho gaye, is liye jawab positive aaya.
Dhyan dein: yahan do minus hain; ek bhi chhoot gaya to jawab ka sign ulta ho jayega.

Wapas \(x\) likhein aur simple karein
\[= \left(1+\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{-1} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\frac{x+1}{x}} + c = \dfrac{x}{x+1} + c\]
Kyun: \(1 + \frac{1}{x}\) ko ek fraction \(\frac{x+1}{x}\) likha; power \(-1\) ka matlab ulta (reciprocal) karna hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x}{x+1}\right) = \dfrac{(x+1) - x}{(x+1)^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}\]
Integrand: \((1+\frac{1}{x})^{-2}\frac{1}{x^{2}} = \frac{x^{2}}{(x+1)^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{x^{2}} = \frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}\). Dono barabar hain, yani jawab sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Answer key \(-\frac{1}{3}\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^{3} + c\) likhti hai. Yeh \(\int (1+\frac{1}{x})^{2}\frac{1}{x^{2}}\,dx\) (power \(+2\)) ka jawab hai, chhape hue sawal (power \(-2\)) ka nahi.
Chhape hue sawal ka sahi jawab \(\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^{-1} + c = \frac{x}{x+1} + c\) hai; upar ki tasdeeq yahi dikhati hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{(1+\sqrt{x})^{5}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan \((1+\sqrt{x})\) ki power 5 hai aur poora \(\sqrt{x}\) se divide ho raha hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral; \(x > 0\) samajhna hai warna \(\sqrt{x}\) real nahi.
Socho: \(1+\sqrt{x}\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\) hai, aur integrand mein \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\) pehle se baitha hai.
Bas 2 ka constant adjust karna hoga.
Plan: \(u = 1+\sqrt{x}\), phir \(\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,du\) aur power rule.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{(1+\sqrt{x})^{5}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\), \(x > 0\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: substitution \(u = 1+\sqrt{x}\). Wajah: is ke derivative mein \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\) aata hai jo integrand mein maujood hai.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = 1 + \sqrt{x}\]
\[du = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,dx\]
\[\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,du\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x} = x^{1/2}\), is ka derivative \(\frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\). Dono taraf 2 se multiply kiya to \(\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}}\) akela reh gaya.

Integral ko \(u\) mein likh kar hal karein
\[\int u^{5}\cdot 2\,du = 2\cdot\dfrac{u^{6}}{6} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}u^{6} + c\]
Kyun: power rule, \(n = 5\). \(\frac{2}{6}\) simplify ho kar \(\frac{1}{3}\) bana.
Dhyan dein: yahan 2 multiply hota hai, divide nahi; \(du\) mein \(\frac{1}{2}\) tha, is liye \(dx/\sqrt{x}\) mein 2 aaya.

Wapas \(x\) likhein
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}(1+\sqrt{x})^{6} + c\]
Kyun: jawab \(x\) mein dena hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{3}(1+\sqrt{x})^{6}\Big]\]
\[= 2(1+\sqrt{x})^{5}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{(1+\sqrt{x})^{5}}{\sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: chain rule se asal integrand wapas mil gaya.

blocks.prompt: 1 (v) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int (7-x^{5})^{4}\,x^{4}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan bracket \((7-x^{5})\) ki power 4 hai aur saath \(x^{4}\) multiply hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Andar wale ka derivative: \(7-x^{5}\) ka derivative \(-5x^{4}\). Integrand mein \(x^{4}\) maujood hai, sirf \(-5\) ka farq.
Is liye substitution bilkul fit hai.
Plan: \(u = 7-x^{5}\), \(x^{4}dx = -\frac{du}{5}\), phir power rule.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int (7-x^{5})^{4}x^{4}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: substitution \(u = 7-x^{5}\), kyunke is ka derivative \(-5x^{4}\) integrand ke \(x^{4}\) se sirf constant mein mukhtalif hai.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = 7 - x^{5}\]
\[du = -5x^{4}\,dx\]
\[x^{4}\,dx = -\dfrac{du}{5}\]
Kyun: 7 constant hai, us ka derivative zero; \(x^{5}\) ka derivative \(5x^{4}\), aur aage minus tha to \(-5x^{4}\).

Integral ko \(u\) mein likh kar hal karein
\[\int u^{4}\left(-\dfrac{du}{5}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{5}\cdot\dfrac{u^{5}}{5} + c\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{25}u^{5} + c\]
Kyun: power rule \(n = 4\): power 5 hui aur 5 se divide.
Dhyan dein: minus sign \(-5x^{4}\) se aaya hai; isay bhool gaye to jawab \(+\frac{1}{25}(7-x^{5})^{5}\) aayega jo ghalat hai.

Wapas \(x\) likhein
\[= -\dfrac{1}{25}(7-x^{5})^{5} + c\]
Kyun: jawab \(x\) mein chahiye.

blocks.prompt: 1 (vi) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{t^{2}-2t}{(t^{3}-3t^{2}+5)^{4}}\,dt\)
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal ka variable \(x\) nahi balke \(t\) hai; is liye \(dt\) likha hai. Rules bilkul wahi hain.
Denominator mein cubic \(t^{3}-3t^{2}+5\) ki power 4 hai, upar \(t^{2}-2t\).
Cubic ka derivative: \(3t^{2}-6t = 3(t^{2}-2t)\). Yeh numerator ka teen guna hai!
Jab kisi bracket ka derivative numerator ka constant multiple ho, substitution ka signal hai.
Plan: \(u = t^{3}-3t^{2}+5\), \((t^{2}-2t)dt = \frac{du}{3}\), power rule \(n = -4\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{t^{2}-2t}{(t^{3}-3t^{2}+5)^{4}}\,dt\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral (\(t\) mein).
Tareeqa: bracket ko \(u\) banayenge, kyunke us ka derivative numerator ka constant multiple hai.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = t^{3}-3t^{2}+5\]
\[du = (3t^{2}-6t)\,dt = 3(t^{2}-2t)\,dt\]
\[(t^{2}-2t)\,dt = \dfrac{du}{3}\]
Kyun: \(3t^{2}-6t\) mein 3 common nikala to numerator \(t^{2}-2t\) saamne aa gaya.

\(u\) mein likh kar hal karein
\[\dfrac{1}{3}\int u^{-4}\,du = \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{u^{-3}}{-3} + c\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{9}u^{-3} + c\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{u^{4}} = u^{-4}\); power rule mein \(-4 + 1 = -3\) aur \(-3\) se divide.

Wapas \(t\) likhein
\[= -\dfrac{1}{9}(t^{3}-3t^{2}+5)^{-3} + c\]
Kyun: sawal \(t\) mein tha, jawab bhi \(t\) mein.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\Big[-\tfrac{1}{9}u^{-3}\Big] = \tfrac{1}{3}u^{-4}\cdot\dfrac{du}{dt}\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{3}u^{-4}\cdot 3(t^{2}-2t)\]
\[= \dfrac{t^{2}-2t}{(t^{3}-3t^{2}+5)^{4}}\]
Kyun: chain rule se integrand wapas mila, jawab sahi hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (vii) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{\sec^{2}x}{\tan x\cdot\ln\tan x}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein denominator mein \(\tan x\) aur \(\ln\tan x\) dono hain, upar \(\sec^{2}x\).
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Sochiye \(\ln\tan x\) ka derivative kya hai: chain rule se \(\frac{1}{\tan x}\cdot\sec^{2}x\). Yeh integrand ka baqi hissa bilkul yahi hai!
To \(u = \ln\tan x\) rakhte hi integral \(\int\frac{du}{u}\) ban jayega.
Plan: substitution, phir Rule 4 \((\int\frac{du}{u} = \ln|u|)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{\sec^{2}x}{\tan x\,\ln\tan x}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(u = \ln\tan x\), phir Rule 4: \(\int\frac{du}{u} = \ln|u| + c\). Wajah: \(\ln\tan x\) ka derivative integrand mein poora maujood hai.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = \ln\tan x\]
\[du = \dfrac{1}{\tan x}\cdot\sec^{2}x\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\ln\) ka derivative: \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln f = \frac{f'}{f}\). Yahan \(f = \tan x\), \(f' = \sec^{2}x\).

Integral ko \(u\) mein likhein
\[\int \dfrac{1}{\ln\tan x}\cdot\dfrac{\sec^{2}x}{\tan x}\,dx = \int\dfrac{du}{u}\]
Kyun: integrand ko do hisson mein toda: \(\frac{1}{\ln\tan x}\) jo \(\frac{1}{u}\) hai, aur \(\frac{\sec^{2}x}{\tan x}dx\) jo poora \(du\) hai.

Integrate karein aur \(x\) wapas likhein
\[= \ln|u| + c\]
\[= \ln|\ln\tan x| + c\]
Kyun: \(\int\frac{du}{u} = \ln|u| + c\). Modulus is liye ke \(\ln\) sirf positive number ka hota hai.
Dhyan dein: yahan do \(\ln\) aate hain, ek doosre ke andar; ek \(\ln\) likh dena aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln|\ln\tan x| = \dfrac{1}{\ln\tan x}\cdot\dfrac{\sec^{2}x}{\tan x}\]
Kyun: chain rule do martaba lagaya aur asal integrand wapas aa gaya.

blocks.prompt: 1 (viii) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt{1+\sin 2x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Pehli nazar mein yeh mushkil lagta hai kyunke neeche square root hai.
Lekin \(1 + \sin 2x\) asal mein ek perfect square chhupaye baitha hai: \((\sin x + \cos x)^{2}\).
Root hat jaye to neeche \(\sin x + \cos x\) bachta hai, aur us ka derivative \(\cos x - \sin x\) hai, jo numerator ka minus hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: pehle root ko simple karna, phir \(u = \sin x + \cos x\) aur Rule 4.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt{1+\sin 2x}}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(1 = \sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x\) aur \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\) likh kar perfect square banayenge, phir substitution.

Root ko simple karein
\[1 + \sin 2x = \sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x + 2\sin x\cos x\]
\[= (\sin x + \cos x)^{2}\]
\[\sqrt{1+\sin 2x} = |\sin x + \cos x|\]
Kyun: \(a^{2} + b^{2} + 2ab = (a+b)^{2}\) wala formula, \(a = \sin x\), \(b = \cos x\). Kisi square ka root modulus deta hai: \(\sqrt{p^{2}} = |p|\). Hum woh interval lete hain jahan \(\sin x + \cos x > 0\) (kitab ka jawab bhi isi ke liye hai), to root \(= \sin x + \cos x\).
Dhyan dein: \(1\) ko \(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x\) likhna is sawal ki chaabi hai; yeh trick yaad rakhiye.

Integral ab yeh ban gaya
\[\int \dfrac{\sin x - \cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}\,dx\]
Kyun: root khatam ho gaya, ab seedha fraction hai.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = \sin x + \cos x\]
\[du = (\cos x - \sin x)\,dx\]
\[(\sin x - \cos x)\,dx = -du\]
Kyun: \(\sin x\) ka derivative \(\cos x\), \(\cos x\) ka derivative \(-\sin x\). Numerator is ka bilkul ulta (minus) hai.

Integrate karein
\[\int \dfrac{-du}{u} = -\ln|u| + c\]
\[= -\ln|\sin x + \cos x| + c\]
Kyun: Rule 4, \(\int\frac{du}{u} = \ln|u|\), aur minus bahar. (Agar kisi interval mein \(\sin x + \cos x < 0\) ho to root \(-(\sin x + \cos x)\) banta hai aur yahi kaam \(+\ln|\sin x + \cos x| + c\) deta hai.)

Tasdeeq (jahan \(\sin x + \cos x > 0\))
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\big[-\ln|\sin x + \cos x|\big]\]
\[= -\dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{\sin x + \cos x}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin x - \cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}\]
Kyun: yeh wahi integrand hai jo root simple karne ke baad mila tha.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ix) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{\tan^{3}x}{\sec^{4}x+\tan^{4}x}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein \(\tan\) aur \(\sec\) ki powers mili hui hain; seedha \(u\) nazar nahi aata.
Aisi soorat mein sab se pehla qadam: sab kuch \(\sin\) aur \(\cos\) mein badal do.
Upar neeche \(\cos^{4}x\) se multiply karein to integrand \(\frac{\sin^{3}x\cos x}{1+\sin^{4}x}\) ban jata hai.
Ab denominator \(1+\sin^{4}x\) ka derivative \(4\sin^{3}x\cos x\) hai, jo numerator ka 4 guna hai.
Plan: \(\cos^{4}x\) se multiply, phir \(u = 1+\sin^{4}x\) aur Rule 4.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{\tan^{3}x}{\sec^{4}x+\tan^{4}x}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: pehle \(\sin x\), \(\cos x\) mein likhenge, phir denominator ko \(u\) banayenge.

Upar neeche \(\cos^{4}x\) se multiply karein
\[\tan^{3}x\cos^{4}x = \dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\cos^{3}x}\cos^{4}x\]
\[= \sin^{3}x\cos x\]
\[(\sec^{4}x + \tan^{4}x)\cos^{4}x = 1 + \sin^{4}x\]
Kyun: \(\sec x\cos x = 1\) aur \(\tan x\cos x = \sin x\). Kisi fraction ke upar aur neeche ek hi cheez se multiply karne se fraction ki value nahi badalti, sirf shakal badalti hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos^{4}x\) hi kyun? Kyunke denominator mein sab se oonchi power 4 hai; is se saare \(\sec\) khatam ho jate hain.

Integral ab yeh hai
\[\int \dfrac{\sin^{3}x\cos x}{1 + \sin^{4}x}\,dx\]
Kyun: ab sab kuch \(\sin x\) mein hai aur ek \(\cos x\) bacha hai jo \(du\) ke kaam aayega.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = 1 + \sin^{4}x\]
\[du = 4\sin^{3}x\cos x\,dx\]
\[\sin^{3}x\cos x\,dx = \dfrac{du}{4}\]
Kyun: chain rule: \(\sin^{4}x\) ka derivative \(4\sin^{3}x\cdot\cos x\).

Integrate karein
\[\dfrac{1}{4}\int\dfrac{du}{u} = \dfrac{1}{4}\ln|u| + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{4}\ln(1 + \sin^{4}x) + c\]
Kyun: Rule 4. \(1 + \sin^{4}x\) hamesha positive hai, is liye modulus ki zaroorat nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{4}\ln(1+\sin^{4}x)\Big] = \dfrac{\sin^{3}x\cos x}{1+\sin^{4}x}\]
Kyun: yeh wahi integrand hai jo pehle qadam ke baad bana tha.

blocks.prompt: 1 (x) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{x}{1+x\tan x}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Denominator mein \(\tan x\) hai jo kaam ko mushkil bana raha hai.
Trick: upar neeche \(\cos x\) se multiply karo; \(\tan x\cos x = \sin x\) ho jayega.
Phir denominator \(\cos x + x\sin x\) banta hai, aur product rule se is ka derivative \(x\cos x\) nikalta hai, jo naya numerator hai!
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: \(\cos x\) se multiply, \(u = \cos x + x\sin x\), Rule 4.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{x}{1+x\tan x}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: numerator ko denominator ka derivative bana denge, phir Rule 4 \((\int\frac{f'}{f} = \ln|f|)\).

Upar neeche \(\cos x\) se multiply karein
\[\dfrac{x}{1+x\tan x} = \dfrac{x\cos x}{\cos x + x\sin x}\]
Kyun: \(1\cdot\cos x = \cos x\) aur \(x\tan x\cos x = x\sin x\). Fraction ki value wahi rehti hai.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = \cos x + x\sin x\]
\[du = (-\sin x + \sin x + x\cos x)\,dx\]
\[du = x\cos x\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\cos x\) ka derivative \(-\sin x\); \(x\sin x\) par product rule: \(1\cdot\sin x + x\cos x\). \(-\sin x\) aur \(+\sin x\) cancel ho gaye.
Dhyan dein: \(x\sin x\) ka derivative sirf \(x\cos x\) likhna ghalat hai; product rule mein do terms aate hain.

Integrate karein
\[\int\dfrac{du}{u} = \ln|u| + c\]
\[= \ln|\cos x + x\sin x| + c\]
Kyun: Rule 4.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln|\cos x + x\sin x| = \dfrac{x\cos x}{\cos x + x\sin x}\]
Upar neeche \(\cos x\) se divide karein to \(\frac{x}{1 + x\tan x}\) milta hai, yani asal integrand.

blocks.prompt: 1 (xi) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{\ln\sec x}{\cot x}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Pehle \(\cot x\) se divide ko seedha karte hain: \(\cot x\) se divide karna \(\tan x\) se multiply karna hai.
Integral ban gaya \(\int \tan x\,\ln\sec x\,dx\).
Ab dekhiye: \(\ln\sec x\) ka derivative \(\frac{\sec x\tan x}{\sec x} = \tan x\). Yani \(\tan x\,dx\) poora \(du\) hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: \(u = \ln\sec x\), phir \(\int u\,du\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{\ln\sec x}{\cot x}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(\frac{1}{\cot x} = \tan x\) likh kar \(u = \ln\sec x\) rakhenge.

Integrand ko dobara likhein
\[\int \dfrac{\ln\sec x}{\cot x}\,dx = \int \tan x\,\ln\sec x\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\tan x\) aur \(\cot x\) ek doosre ke reciprocal hain.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = \ln\sec x\]
\[du = \dfrac{\sec x\tan x}{\sec x}\,dx = \tan x\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\ln f\) ka derivative \(\frac{f'}{f}\); \(\sec x\) ka derivative \(\sec x\tan x\). \(\sec x\) cancel ho gaya.

Integrate karein
\[\int u\,du = \dfrac{u^{2}}{2} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}(\ln\sec x)^{2} + c\]
Kyun: power rule \(n = 1\).

Answer key wali shakal
\[\ln\sec x = \ln\dfrac{1}{\cos x} = -\ln\cos x\]
\[\dfrac{1}{2}(\ln\sec x)^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}(\ln\cos x)^{2}\]
Kyun: \(\ln\frac{1}{a} = -\ln a\), aur square karne se minus khatam ho jata hai. Is liye kitab ka \(\frac{1}{2}(\ln\cos x)^{2}\) bhi bilkul sahi hai.
Dhyan dein: dono jawab dekhne mein alag hain magar barabar hain; ghabrayein nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{2}(\ln\sec x)^{2}\Big] = \ln\sec x\cdot\tan x\]
Kyun: yeh \(\frac{\ln\sec x}{\cot x}\) hi hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (xii) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{\ln(\sin x)}{\tan x}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh part (xi) ka bhai hai.
\(\tan x\) se divide karna \(\cot x\) se multiply karna hai.
Aur \(\ln\sin x\) ka derivative \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \cot x\) hai, jo integrand mein maujood hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: \(u = \ln\sin x\), phir \(\int u\,du\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{\ln(\sin x)}{\tan x}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(\frac{1}{\tan x} = \cot x\), phir \(u = \ln\sin x\); wajah yeh ke is ka derivative \(\cot x\) hai.

Dobara likhein aur \(u\) chunein
\[\int \cot x\,\ln(\sin x)\,dx\]
\[u = \ln\sin x,\quad du = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\,dx = \cot x\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\ln f\) ka derivative \(\frac{f'}{f}\), yahan \(f = \sin x\), \(f' = \cos x\).

Integrate karein
\[\int u\,du = \dfrac{u^{2}}{2} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}(\ln\sin x)^{2} + c\]
Kyun: power rule \(n = 1\).
Dhyan dein: \((\ln\sin x)^{2}\) aur \(\ln(\sin^{2}x)\) alag cheezein hain; bracket sahi jagah lagayein.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{2}(\ln\sin x)^{2}\Big] = \ln\sin x\cdot\cot x\]
Kyun: yeh \(\frac{\ln\sin x}{\tan x}\) hi hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (xiii) Evaluate the following integral (by using suitable substitution): \(\int \frac{e^{2x}}{(2+e^{2x})^{2}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Denominator mein \((2 + e^{2x})\) ka square hai, upar \(e^{2x}\).
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
\(2 + e^{2x}\) ka derivative \(2e^{2x}\) hai; numerator mein \(e^{2x}\) hai, sirf 2 ka farq.
Yeh phir wahi pehchana hua pattern hai: bracket ko \(u\) banao.
Plan: \(u = 2 + e^{2x}\), \(e^{2x}dx = \frac{du}{2}\), power rule \(n = -2\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{e^{2x}}{(2+e^{2x})^{2}}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: substitution \(u = 2 + e^{2x}\), kyunke us ka derivative numerator ka 2 guna hai.

\(u\) chunein
\[u = 2 + e^{2x}\]
\[du = 2e^{2x}\,dx\]
\[e^{2x}\,dx = \dfrac{du}{2}\]
Kyun: \(e^{2x}\) ka derivative chain rule se \(e^{2x}\cdot 2\).

Integrate karein
\[\dfrac{1}{2}\int u^{-2}\,du = \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{u^{-1}}{-1} + c\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{2u} + c\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{u^{2}} = u^{-2}\), power rule se \(-2+1 = -1\).
Dhyan dein: yahan \(\ln\) nahi aata; \(\ln\) sirf tab aata hai jab power bilkul \(-1\) ho, yahan \(-2\) hai.

Wapas \(x\) likhein
\[= -\dfrac{1}{2(2 + e^{2x})} + c\]
Kyun: jawab \(x\) mein.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[-\tfrac{1}{2}(2+e^{2x})^{-1}\Big]\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{2}(2+e^{2x})^{-2}\cdot 2e^{2x}\]
\[= \dfrac{e^{2x}}{(2+e^{2x})^{2}}\]
Kyun: integrand wapas mil gaya.
